newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives would not join EMU in 1999 - Lamont.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives would not join EMU in 1999 - Lamont.

text.p: The Conservative Party conference this week has made it clear Britain would not join a European single currency in 1999 if the party remained in power, former Chancellor of the Exchequer Norman Lamont said.

Speaking at a fringe meeting at the conference on Wednesday, Lamont, who is strongly opposed to the single currency, said: "There is no prospect of the Conservative Party joining a single currency in the first wave."
"That should be clear to everyone from this conference," Lamont, who was Britain's finance minister until May 1993, added.
The conference has seen a series of appeals from the party's "Eurosceptics" to Prime Minister John Major to rule out joining a single currency before a general election, due within months.

Lamont made a strong attack on advocates of greater European integration, saying they should be more honest about where they wanted to lead Britain. "You cannot say that the transfer of sovereignty to Europe is inevitable and desirable, and also say that there is no prospect of a federal Europe," he said.
Indicating he believed it might become necessary to consider whether Britain should leave Europe, he added: "If Europe does not change, membership will not be worth having."
Speaking at the same meeting, Leon Brittan, the former Conservative cabinet minister who is now a European Union commissioner, continued his attacks on Eurosceptics.
He said they were criticising countries such as France and Germany for trimming budget deficits in the same way that Conservative governments had done in the past.
"Just when we are starting to win the battle for ideas in Europe, the Eurosceptics want us to abandon the ground we have won and start arguing for inflationary policies across Europe," he said.
